description: Pointsman is a decision service on Cloudflare Workers. A client system sends a state (a resident's road report, a new issue, a deploy's stack events) to `POST /v1/decide/{profile}`; a language model answers the profile's typed questions; the profile's rules turn the answers into an action (`auto`, `review` or a custom one); every decision is logged with its profile version and model. One Worker per integrator, deployed from a private config repository that holds the profiles. Clients: the FIWARE bridge, two GitHub Actions and MCP agents. The state author is the untrusted surface; token holders are trusted for their profiles; the operator is trusted.

trust_boundaries.boundary: `engine-api`: a finding matters if it is reachable from a request that carries a valid token, or from the `state`, `ref` or `callback_url` such a request carries, or from a model backend's response. A finding that needs an invalid or missing token to succeed is a finding against `P-AUTH-REQUIRED` (§1.11).
trust_boundaries.reachability_precondition: reachable from a request with a valid token, from the state, ref or callback_url it carries, or from a model backend response

trust_boundaries.boundary: `engine-facts`: reachable from the geometry at a profile's `at` path in the client's state, from the pull request (`repo`, `number`, `head`) at a GitHub fact's `at` path, or from a tile, routing or GitHub API response.
trust_boundaries.reachability_precondition: reachable from the geometry at a profile's `at` path in the client's state, from the pull request (repo, number, head) at a GitHub fact's `at` path, or from a tile, routing or GitHub API response

trust_boundaries.boundary: `engine-callbacks`: reachable from `callback_url` and from the receiver's response.
trust_boundaries.reachability_precondition: reachable from callback_url or from the receiver's response

trust_boundaries.boundary: `engine-mcp`: reachable from an MCP tool call with a valid API token or OAuth access token, or from the OAuth routes before login (consent page, client registration, GitHub callback).
trust_boundaries.reachability_precondition: reachable from an MCP tool call with a valid API token or OAuth access token, or from the OAuth routes before login

trust_boundaries.boundary: `bridge`: reachable from a notification that carries the shared secret, from the entity bodies in it, from a queue message, or from a broker or Pointsman response; the broker's entity writers are the untrusted side, the broker itself and Pointsman are trusted collaborators
trust_boundaries.reachability_precondition: reachable from a notification carrying the shared secret, from the entities in it, from a queue message, or from a broker or Pointsman response

trust_boundaries.boundary: `action-triage`: reachable from the issue title and body in the event payload, or from Pointsman's response.
trust_boundaries.reachability_precondition: reachable from the issue title and body in the event payload, or from Pointsman's response

trust_boundaries.boundary: `action-deploy-watch`: reachable from CloudFormation stack events or from Pointsman's response. The `run` command and the stack names come from the workflow and are trusted.
trust_boundaries.reachability_precondition: reachable from CloudFormation stack events or from Pointsman's response; run and stacks are trusted workflow inputs

trust_boundaries.boundary: `config-repo`: reachable from a pull request to the config repository or from the operator's own command line; both are trusted authors (§1.7).
trust_boundaries.reachability_precondition: reachable from a pull request to the config repository or from the operator's command line; both are trusted authors

known_misuse.pattern: acting on a test: true decision as if it were logged
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Acting on a `test: true` decision as if it were logged (`R-IGNORE-TEST-DECISIONS`).
known_misuse.instead: check the test field; keep test tokens out of production clients

known_misuse.pattern: reading p as the model's accuracy and setting thresholds without a margin
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Reading `p` as "the model is 90 % accurate" and setting thresholds without a margin (`D-MODEL-ACCURACY`).
known_misuse.instead: treat p as the model's probability; keep a margin; re-check examples after model updates

known_misuse.pattern: citing the decision log as proof that a report was true or that a named person resolved it
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Citing the decision log as proof that a report was true or that a named person resolved it (`D-LOG-TRUTH`, `D-REVIEWER-IDENTITY`).
known_misuse.instead: treat the log as the engine's record; authenticate people in the client

known_misuse.pattern: one --profiles '*' token shared by every client
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Using one `--profiles '*'` token for every client, so the log cannot tell clients apart and a leak exposes every profile (`R-SCOPED-TOKENS`).

known_misuse.pattern: building deploy-watch's run or stacks from issue or pull-request text
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Building deploy-watch's `run` or `stacks` from issue or pull-request text (`R-ACTION-INPUTS`).
known_misuse.instead: set them in the workflow only

known_misuse.pattern: a callback receiver that acts without checking the signature and timestamp, or that is not idempotent
known_misuse.why_unsafe: A callback receiver that acts on the payload without checking the signature and timestamp, or that is not idempotent (`R-VERIFY-CALLBACK`).
known_misuse.instead: verify the HMAC and timestamp; dedupe on decision_id

known_misuse.pattern: a subscription that limits notification.attributes to the inputs so the result attribute never arrives and every notification decides again
known_misuse.why_unsafe: A bridge subscription that limits `notification.attributes` to the inputs, so the result attribute never arrives and every notification decides again (`R-BRIDGE-SUBSCRIPTION`).
known_misuse.instead: leave notification.attributes unset or include the result attribute

known_misuse.pattern: mcp.visible: true on a profile whose questions or decisions are not for every organization member
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Setting `mcp.visible: true` on a profile whose questions or decisions are not for every organization member (`R-MCP-VISIBLE`).

known_misuse.pattern: putting secrets or identifying free text into ref
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Putting secrets or an identifying free text into `ref` (`R-STATE-IS-DATA`).
known_misuse.instead: use an opaque reference such as an issue URL

known_misuse.pattern: sending personal data in state with the AI Gateway's logs on and no retention decision
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Sending personal data in `state` with the AI Gateway's logs on and no retention decision (`R-DATA-MINIMISATION`).
known_misuse.instead: set collect_logs: false or decide retention first

known_misuse.pattern: making a consequential action the policy's default so a missing fact or a steered answer falls through to it
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Making a consequential action (`publish`, `cancel`) the policy's default action, so a missing fact or a steered answer falls through to it (`R-REVIEW-PATH`).

known_misuse.pattern: giving the GitHub fact credential write permissions, or a classic token that reaches every repository of its owner
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Giving the GitHub fact credential write permissions, or a classic token that reaches every repository of its owner, so a leaked Worker secret can change repositories (`R-GITHUB-CREDENTIAL`, `R-GITHUB-REPOSITORIES`).
known_misuse.instead: a fine-grained token or GitHub App with read permissions on the repositories the deployment decides about

known_misuse.pattern: an allowing rule that counts on an earlier blocking rule while GitHub facts can be missing, or a glob such as *.md meant to cover every folder
known_misuse.why_unsafe: An allowing rule that counts on an earlier blocking rule while GitHub facts can be missing, or a glob such as `*.md` that was meant to cover every folder (`R-GITHUB-POSITIVE-RULES`).
known_misuse.instead: check missing facts first; write allowing conditions as known positive values; use **/*.md for every folder

known_misuse.pattern: reading github_checks.green as proof that the intended jobs ran when required checks are matched by name only
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Reading `github_checks.green` as proof that the intended jobs ran when the required checks are matched by name only (`D-GITHUB-CHECK-NAMES`, `R-GITHUB-RULES`).
known_misuse.instead: require checks as ruleset workflows or tie them to their app

known_misuse.pattern: using author_sole_code_owner to skip a review while CODEOWNERS itself is not protected on the base branch
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Using `author_sole_code_owner` to skip a review while `CODEOWNERS` itself is not protected on the base branch, so whoever merges a change to it decides who is the only owner (`D-FACT-DATA-AS-PUBLISHED`).
known_misuse.instead: protect CODEOWNERS on the base branch, for example with a code-owner review for changes to it

known_misuse.pattern: acting on a decision for a later push of the same pull request
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Acting on a decision for a later push of the same pull request (`R-GITHUB-ACT-ON-HEAD`).
known_misuse.instead: act only for the head commit the request named; decide again after a push

known_non_findings.reported_as: API tokens are hashed with plain SHA-256 instead of a slow password hash
known_non_findings.why_safe: Covers engine-api, config-repo; symptom 'credential-storage-weakness'. Exact-match conditions (§1.15): the report concerns `TOKENS` records written by `scripts/tokens.mjs`; the token in question is a `pm_` token of 32 random bytes.
known_non_findings.suppression: TOKENS records written by scripts/tokens.mjs; the token is a pm_ token of 32 random bytes

known_non_findings.reported_as: a revoked token still works for up to a minute
known_non_findings.why_safe: Covers engine-api, engine-mcp; symptom 'stale-authentication'. Exact-match conditions (§1.15): the token was revoked through `scripts/tokens.mjs revoke` less than about 60 seconds before the accepted request.
known_non_findings.suppression: revoked through scripts/tokens.mjs revoke less than about 60 seconds before the accepted request

known_non_findings.reported_as: a person removed from the GitHub organization can still use MCP
known_non_findings.why_safe: Covers engine-mcp; symptom 'stale-authorization'. Exact-match conditions (§1.15): the grant was issued while the person was an active member; less than 7 days have passed; no new login happened.
known_non_findings.suppression: grant issued while an active member; less than 7 days passed; no new login

known_non_findings.why_safe: Covers engine-callbacks; symptom 'duplicate-delivery'. Exact-match conditions (§1.15): the receiver did not answer 2xx within 10 s on the first attempt, or its 2xx was lost; the payloads are identical.
known_non_findings.suppression: no 2xx within 10 s on the first attempt or the 2xx was lost; identical payloads

known_non_findings.reported_as: the full state is visible in the AI Gateway logs although the decision log stores only a hash
known_non_findings.why_safe: Covers engine-api, engine-mcp; symptom 'information-disclosure'. Exact-match conditions (§1.15): the deployment sets `AI_GATEWAY_ID` and the gateway has `collect_logs: true`.

known_non_findings.reported_as: untrusted issue text flows from the event payload to GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY or GITHUB_OUTPUT
known_non_findings.why_safe: Covers action-triage; symptom 'taint-flow-to-sink'. Exact-match conditions (§1.15): the flagged values are the answers, probabilities, labels or decision id; the issue title and body are not among them.
known_non_findings.suppression: the flagged values are answers, probabilities, labels or the decision id; the issue title and body are not among them

known_non_findings.reported_as: text in the state made the model answer X and the policy acted on that well-formed answer
known_non_findings.why_safe: Covers engine-api, engine-mcp, bridge, action-triage, action-deploy-watch; symptom 'prompt-injection-steered-answer'. Exact-match conditions (§1.15): every answer is inside the profile's types and options; the action is the one the policy produces for those answers; no answer outside the set and no action outside the profile's set (either would be `VALID` against `P-ANSWER-SHAPE` or `P-ACTION-FROM-POLICY`).
known_non_findings.suppression: every answer inside the profile's types and options; the action is the one the policy produces for those answers; no answer outside the set and no action outside the profile's set

known_non_findings.reported_as: a token holder can make the engine POST to any public https URL
known_non_findings.why_safe: Covers engine-callbacks; symptom 'ssrf-to-public-host'. Exact-match conditions (§1.15): the URL is public and https; the payload is the signed final answer; no private or loopback address was reached and no redirect was followed (either would be `VALID` against `P-OUTBOUND-PUBLIC-ONLY`).
known_non_findings.suppression: the URL is public and https; the payload is the signed final answer; no private or loopback address reached and no redirect followed
